_comment: 3D diffusive cube (Sigma_t 100 over cells of width 0.1, scattering ratio 0.99) on a deliberately anisotropic 20x10x5 box - 2 x 1 x 0.5 - with the two Y faces reflective and the other four vacuum. This is the face-convention pin: in 3D bottom/top are the Z faces and the Y ones are front/back, so a DSA operator that mixed the two axes up would put a Marshak condition where the transport has reflection and a zero-Neumann one where it has vacuum. The box being anisotropic is what makes that visible - it costs three extra iterations, measured, where a cubic box would hide it behind the symmetry.
